The country speaks Mandarin (Putonghua) and uses the Chinese yuan (renminbi). varied continental This database profiles the nation completely: its people, land, government, economy, history, landmarks, food, festivals, customs, and nature — everything a student, traveler, or curious reader needs for a full picture.

title: Climate

title: Government
description: China is governed as a socialist republic. The system of government shapes daily life through laws, services, and the citizen's relationship to the state. Its modern form dates to 1949 (PRC) — and like all governments, it continues to evolve with its people.

title: Independence and statehood
description: Statehood in China: 1949 (PRC). National days, flags, and anthems all trace to the moment of independence or founding — the story every schoolchild learns. Understanding it explains the country's pride, its holidays, and often its friendships and rivalries.

title: Languages
description: Language in China: Mandarin (Putonghua). Language carries the culture's humor, proverbs, and worldview — learning even greetings opens doors that stay closed to outsiders. Multilingual countries code-switch daily; visitors who try the local tongue are repaid with warmth.

title: Currency and money
description: Money in China: the Chinese yuan (renminbi). Travelers should learn the denominations, the tipping customs, and whether cards or cash rule daily life. Exchange rates move, but the habit of checking prices in local terms keeps budgets honest.

title: Peking duck
description: Peking duck: The lacquered icon.. Peking duck is China's food at its most beloved: generations perfected it, regions argue over it, and everyone who leaves home craves it. Order it where the locals order it; the best version is rarely the fanciest.
